source.statement: T-abs-nested-converse: CurveNestedOn C C' ⊤ gives LeNested C C' when C is causally arc-connected (CurveNestedOn.leNested_of_causallyArcConnected); if the last step needs C' arc-connected too, add it and report

[[open]] curve_nested → le_nested: 'True when C is causally arc-connected (x ≤_U y of C lies on a C-causal curve of U, which is C'-causal by curve nesting on U, so x ≤_U y for C'), not in Lean either'

hypotheses.note: the ladder node Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnected; only its ≤ half is used (a C-causal curve of U over [0,1] through each x ≤_U y). The open form asks C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W and curve nesting on W only.

hypotheses.note: a C'-causal curve of U from x to y gives x ≤_U y for C' in every causality (Causality.CausalCurveOn.le_of_le, Causal/Curves.lean:253); and it would not help in place of the hypothesis on C: the spacelike line is causally arc-connected (label 2-bare)
CurveNestedOn C C' ⊤, restricted to U by CurveNestedOn.mono

The witness: (∀ W, CurveNestedOn pointedLine spacelikeLine W) ∧ ¬ LeNested pointedLine spacelikeLine ∧ ¬ pointedLine.CausallyArcConnected ∧ pointedLine.IsCausal ∧ pointedLine.PushUp ∧ spacelikeLine.CausallyArcConnected. consequences.statement: curve nesting at M gives ≤-nesting when the narrower C is causally arc-connected (the converse of le_nested ⇒ curve_nested); on an open W, curve nesting on W is ≤-nesting on the opens of W
consequences.under: causally_arc_connected of C (ladder node); nothing of C'. Open form: Causal.Causality.curveNestedOn_iff_of_causallyArcConnectedOn (C causally arc-connected on W); iff form at M: Causal.Causality.leNested_iff_curveNestedOn_top. Sharp on both sides (comment above the entry): not on C' (Causal.not_leNested_of_curveNested_wider_bare, the spacelike line is causally arc-connected), not weakened to absolutely_minimal of C (Causal.not_leNested_of_curveNested_absolutelyMinimal_bare, the rational line)

consequences.statement: curve nesting on W is transitive (ERS Remark 4.74: C_g ≤ C_b ≤ C_m)
curve nesting is invariant under time reversal: C.dual is curve-nested in C'.dual on W iff C is curve-nested in C' on W

for_keeper.simulation: On a /tmp copy of programme/ladder.toml with the four [[fails]] above added and the three [[open]] entries they settle removed, `tools/ladder.py check --file` reports no contradiction (only 'witness not found', the scaffold being outside the index until graduation) and `matrix` classifies 12 more ordered pairs: curve_nested ⇏ le_nested; absolutely_minimal, is_causal, push_up, locally_push_up ⇏ causally_arc_connected (the last three where unknown), causally_open_future, causally_open.

kb_proposals: A cheap absolutely minimal causality with only constant causal curves: Causal.rationalLine (CausalScaffold.NestedConverse), x ≤_U y iff x = y ∈ U or x < y both rational with [x, y] ⊆ U, ≪ empty. Absolute minimality by equal rational steps below a Lebesgue number (lebesgue_number_lemma_of_metric); constant curves because a non-constant one takes an irrational value (exists_irrational_btwn + intermediate_value_Icc). It is causal, has push-up, and is neither causally arc-connected nor causally open in the future: the first Lean model that is absolutely minimal and not causally open.

Curve nesting and ≤-nesting agree when the narrower causality is causally arc-connected (Causality.leNested_iff_curveNestedOn_top, open form curveNestedOn_iff_of_causallyArcConnectedOn); a line whose causal curves are constant (pointedLine, rationalLine) is curve-nested in every causality of ℝ (pointedLine_curveNestedOn, rationalLine_curveNestedOn), the generic step being Causality.causalCurveOn_of_forall_eq. The spacelike line is causally arc-connected (spacelikeLine_causallyArcConnected).
notes: Layer-1 rule: imports Causal.NestedCausalities and Causal.LinesReachable (their Causal closure, computed: ArcConnected, Cauchy, CauchyExtension, Causality, CompactMinimal, CurveComponents, Curves, CurvesExtend, DependenceDomain, Generated, Geroch, GlobalHyperbolicity, Inextensible, Lines, LinesCurves, LinesReachable, Local, Measure, MeasureRemarks, Minimal, Morphism, NestedCausalities, Properties, PushUp, Reachable, StrongCausality, Subdivision: no Minkowski/Static/SingularFlat/Flat/Model/Port/CBG module) and one mathlib module not previously in the closure, Mathlib.NumberTheory.Real.Irrational (for exists_irrational_btwn; its olean is in the mathlib cache). No metric notion in any statement; the metric of ℝ is used inside the proof of rationalLine_absolutelyMinimal only (Lebesgue number), as Causal.LadderLocal and Causal.NestedCausalities already do on ℝ. `lake build CausalScaffold.NestedConverse` rebuilt only this module; the file also typechecks with -DwarningAsError=true (graduation-ready); #print axioms on the principal theorems: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Labels 1 to 3 are the target; label 4 (the rational line) goes beyond it, as sharpness of 1 and as a witness for two [[open]] ladder entries; the master session may graduate or drop it independently. Names possibly shared with the parallel closers: none of this file's names existed in lean-causal at dispatch time (checked by grep); spacelikeLine_causallyArcConnected is the only spacelike-line lemma added, T-abs-nested-transfer may wish to reuse it. The witness for T-abs-pushup-not-open's push_up ⇏ causally_open_future is independent: the rational line also has push-up and is not causally open in the future, so that target's added value is the local causal openness of its line (locally_causally_open ⇏ causally_open_future).
